card.name: Conditional clauses after "if"
card.fires_on: The word "if" opening a condition, and the next few words inside that condition ("you probably", "someone else", "stores a"). It appears in instructions and advice aimed at a reader or user.

modes.label: The word if
modes.description: "If" starts a sentence or clause that sets a condition, often in instructions or advice.
modes.example: <<If>> a specialist has assessed your child for a

modes.label: Inside the if-clause
modes.description: Words just after "if" or "you" that continue the condition, such as probably, else, or a.
modes.example: If a specialist has assessed your child for a learning problem, you<< probably>> have a report outlining the test results.

card.writes: It lowers second-person words like "your" and "yourself" and favors past-tense narrative verbs, so the text moves away from addressing the reader.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a sentence sets up an "if" condition for the reader.
